name: pcap_extract
description: Export protocol objects from a capture with the installed tshark and index every one. It records the tshark version and the export object types that build lists (an explicitly named type the build does not list is refused by name; the default list is cut to the listed ones and the rest named), runs every pass under ONE shared deadline (a pass that uses it up is killed with everything it started and the rest are not_attempted), and keeps index.tsv and receipt.json from the first moment, replaced after every pass. Each HTTP object is tied to a frame by content only: matched_by_content when its SHA-256 equals exactly one listed response body and no other exported object has it (frame, stream, time, endpoints, host, request URI), ambiguous with the frames listed, or unmapped with the reason; other protocols are indexed and unmapped. That is a statement about equal bytes, not about a session, and an unmapped object is not evidence that it was absent from the capture. If the listing pass fails or cannot be read whole, no frame is claimed. tshark is the only engine used, so agreement with the capture recipe is not independent. SENSITIVE: exported objects, their names and request URIs can carry credentials and tokens. The directory is private (0700/0600, tshark's own files too); a token-shaped object name is moved to withheld-NNNNNN and never printed; a request URI loses user-info, token-shaped path text and query values; the digest of an object under 128 bytes is not written. Run it as a job with secret_output: true; write_values: true (jobs only, refused elsewhere) writes the real names and URIs to $OUT/pcap-extract-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created before anything runs, and a second run in the same job is refused by name.

out_dir.description: An empty directory under work/ (in a job, under $OUT) for the exported objects, index.tsv, receipt.json and _logs/. It is private (0700, files 0600)

protocols.description: Wireshark export object types to run. Default: http, smb, smb2, tftp, imf, cut to the types the installed tshark lists (the rest are named in protocols_skipped_unsupported). A type the build does not list is refused by name and nothing is written

display_filter.description: Optional Wireshark display filter, passed to every pass and to the HTTP listing. Whether the installed build applies it to object export is not established by this tool: check an object you rely on

timeout_seconds.description: One deadline shared by every pass (default 3000, at least 1); a pass that uses it up is killed and the later ones are listed as not_attempted

write_values.description: Write the real names and request URIs of the objects that had one withheld to $OUT/pcap-extract-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the file is created first and one already there is refused; nothing about a short object's digest is ever written
